[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
James was reportedly born about 1773 and died in 1831. His parentage has not been proved. He is currently attached to [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]], but the approximately sixty-five-year gap makes a later generation more likely; the relationship should remain uncertain until a baptism, will or property succession identifies his father.

=== Possible early records ===

A release dated 16 April 1795 concerning garden ground in Newtown of Larne was witnessed by '''James Glasgow of Larne, merchant''', and Charles McGarel, gentleman.<ref name="Merchant1795">Registry of Deeds transcript, release dated 16 April 1795, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-Q9B8-H FamilySearch image].</ref>

An assignment recorded in 1797 concerning a Larne tenement near Charles Dawson Stewart's tanyard includes a witness signature for '''James Glasgow junior'''.<ref name="Junior1797">Registry of Deeds transcript, assignment recorded in 1797, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-Q96R-C FamilySearch image].</ref>

The date, place, merchant designation and use of “junior” fit this James better than the older Larne men. Neither deed names his parents. “Junior” distinguishes him from an older James but does not by itself prove a father-son relationship.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1509]] is assessed at 34% (possible). The later Larne James’s reported 1773 birth fits the older ropemaker’s 1762 marriage better than William’s circa-1708 generation. No held record names his father and the chronology’s stone attribution is inconsistent.

Complete selected father-profile proposition; recorded role and adult identification distinguished below.

Next useful test: Recover the alleged shared stone or a 1773 baptism and trace lease heirs.

Source basis already held: [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Larne/Kilwaughter congregation register chronology]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


[[Glasgow-4024|James Glasgow of Cookstown (abt.1791-bef.1831)]] was buried at St Luran's on 13 March 1831 aged 40. He is not this Larne man: the reported ages, locality and burial context differ. The profiles should remain separate.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

The younger James of Larne remains a provisional identity assembled from the 1795 merchant and 1797 “junior” occurrences. Those records need not identify the same man, and neither names him as the father of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]. He is nevertheless an age-compatible possible son of [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] and a possible route to Alexander's generation: an estimated birth about 1773 would allow ordinary fatherhood ages in the early nineteenth century. This is an alternative to the older-Alexander route, not a replacement for the Thomas-family testimony, and Thomas and Daniel must not be assigned to this James merely to make a pedigree. The ropemaker, this possible merchant/junior identity, and the Larne tanner are distinct record groups unless a document joins them. Preserve the existing record citations and state the identity and kinship as provisional.<ref name="YoungerJamesCurrent">The merchant and junior references cited above establish leads, not a father statement for Alexander.</ref>

=== Additional source context ===

These contextual and comparison sources supplement the individual record assessments above; they do not supply a missing parental statement.
* Related profile: [[Glasgow-3986]].

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, Belfast Juvenile Society secretary, 1830–1831. James Glasgow and Walter Moffat are named secretaries announcing the Belfast Juvenile Society’s sixth annual meeting at Rev. Dr Cooke’s May Street meeting-house on Monday 15 November 1830. In March 1831 Rev. Walter Moffatt and Mr James Glasgow attended a Knockbracken meeting as the Society’s deputation; Rev. Thomas Houston chaired it.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 12 November 1830, p.2, Belfast Juvenile Society sixth annual meeting announcement; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390573239/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 4 March 1831, p.4, Belfast Juvenile Society, Knockbracken meeting; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390543442/ record].</ref> The repeated society and associates support one society account. The same Walter Moffat appears in the 1828 Institution report, making [[Glasgow-1780]] a compatible student/ministry-network candidate; this does not prove that the society secretary is the college student. The newspaper does not call James the president, chair or minister. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, Belfast tobacco seller, 1822–23. James Glasgow offered leaf tobacco in three Belfast advertisements in 1822–23. The August 1822 notice directs buyers to him at James M’Master’s; the May 1823 notice locates samples at M’Master’s North Street premises.<ref>The Irishman, 15 March 1822, p. 2, tobacco advertisement dated 9 March; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/61259036/ record]; The Irishman, 23 August 1822, p. 3, tobacco advertisement dated 20 August; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/61260054/ record]; The Irishman, 30 May 1823, p. 3, tobacco advertisement dated 27 May; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/61261904/ record].</ref> Repeated name, trade and contact support a consolidated seller account. M’Master’s premises are a commercial contact, not a proved home or owned property. No age, family or link to William Glasgow the grocer is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, Belfast tobacco seller, 1822–23. An auction notice describes the large shop and stores at No.32 Rosemary Street, Belfast, as formerly occupied by Mr James Glasgow. The lease interest was offered for sale on 1 April 1828; the notice dated 21 March gives 34 years unexpired from 1 November next and £30 late Irish currency yearly rent.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 1 April 1828, p.3, auction of shop and stores, No.32 Rosemary Street; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390544933/ record].</ref> Former occupancy is explicit; ownership, trade and residence are not. The surname is certain, but identity with the 1822–23 tobacco seller, William the grocer or another James remains unproved. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, Larne freehold applicant, 1830–1831. James Glasgow of Larne is no.16 among persons applying to register freeholds at the Carrickfergus General Quarter Sessions on 13 January 1831. His December 1830 entry describes houses and land in Upper Glenarm, townland of Larne, with a yearly value of £10.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 24 December 1830, p.3, County Antrim freehold-registration applications; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574399/ record].</ref> This is an application published on 24 December 1830, not proof that registration succeeded. [[Glasgow-3986]] is the strongest compatible local candidate, but the notice gives no age, occupation, relatives or bridge to the 1795 merchant or 1797 junior. It does not connect Larne to Lisnagaver. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, plaintiff in Dublin Exchequer, 1820. James Glasgow was plaintiff against Maxwell Lepper and Clotworthy Dobbin in a Court of Exchequer report headed Dublin, 22 June 1820. The defendants’ motion to rescind the contempt process was refused with costs and liberty for the plaintiff to continue process.<ref>The Irishman, 30 June 1820, p. 2, Court of Exchequer, Dublin, 22 June; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/61258711/ record].</ref> The report gives a procedural decision, not final judgment on the dispute, and no age, occupation, residence or relatives for James. George Frederick Moulds is named as plaintiff’s agent. Identity with the later Belfast tobacco seller or any candidate is unproved. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, plaintiff in Dublin Exchequer, 1820. A separate report lists James Glasgow on the petty jury for Friday 1 August 1828. He is a juror, not one of the accused in the following riot-and-assault report.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 5 August 1828, p.4, petty jury, Friday 1 August; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390549197/ record].</ref> The name is James Glasgow, not the automated index’s combined William James Glasgow. No residence, occupation or kin is stated. This remains an unassigned legal occurrence; identity with the 1820 Exchequer plaintiff is unproved. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, plaintiff in Dublin Exchequer, 1820. A report in the Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser states that the parties in cause and cross-cause included Robert Thompson of Newry, the Rev. Mr Walsh of Ballymena, and Mr Barbour of Lisburn; it then says “The following were the Jury” and lists James Glasgow.<ref>Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 3 November 1823, p. 3, trial report and jury list; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050060364/ record].</ref> The original page confirms James Glasgow’s jury role in this reported trial. The newspaper issue is from Dublin, but the inspected passage does not show a court heading or venue. Newry, Ballymena and Lisburn describe other named parties, not the juror. The occurrence is compatible with, but not proved to be the same person as, the James Glasgow on the 1828 Belfast petty jury; identity with the 1820 Exchequer plaintiff is also unproved. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Belfast grocer and tobacco seller, 1820–1828 ===

James Glasgow was plaintiff against Maxwell Lepper and Clotworthy Dobbin in a Court of Exchequer report headed Dublin, 22 June 1820. Belfast tobacco advertisements of March and August 1822 and May 1823 name James Glasgow; the latter two direct buyers to James M’Master’s, North Street. A March 1828 notice offers the shop and stores at 32 Rosemary Street, formerly occupied by James Glasgow. The shared trade and contacts support one Belfast trading cluster, with the plaintiff’s identity less certain.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/61258711/ The Irishman, 30 June 1820, p. 2, Exchequer report headed Dublin, 22 June].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/61259036/ The Irishman, 15 March 1822, p. 2, tobacco advertisement dated Belfast, 9 March].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/61260054/ The Irishman, 23 August 1822, p. 3, tobacco advertisement dated 20 August].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/61261904/ The Irishman, 30 May 1823, p. 3, tobacco advertisement dated 27 May].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390544933/ Belfast News-Letter, 1 April 1828, p. 3, Rosemary Street premises].</ref>

The Larne merchant is a compatible candidate for the Belfast grocer. The two towns’ business associations are not mutually exclusive, but no family or deed yet proves the identification. Rosemary Street numbers 20, 2 and 32 in the directory/advertisement transcriptions remain unreconciled. The plaintiff is the least securely joined part of the cluster.
